question.problem:
In a distribution center, the average weight of shipped packages is $2.5$ kilograms. However, $20%$ of packages weigh no more than $2.3$ kilograms. Assuming that package weights are normally distributed, find the standard deviation, $\sigma ,$ of the package weights, **rounded to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
$kg$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the package weight (in kilograms). Then we have $X∼N(2.5,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X\le 2.3)=0.20.$ Converting $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2.3) & =0.20 \\ P(Z\le \frac{2.3-2.5}{\sigma }) & =0.20 \\ Φ(-\frac{0.2}{\sigma }) & =0.20 \\ -\frac{0.2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.20).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.20)=-0.8416.
$$

Finally then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{0.2}{\sigma } & =-0.8416 \\ \frac{0.2}{\sigma } & =0.8416 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{0.2}{0.8416} \\  & ≈0.24\,\text{kg}.\end{aligned}
$$
